description: Plan templates consumed by `tools-offline-app-dev.py plan <template-id>`. Placeholders {project}, {owner}, {date} are substituted from --set key=value flags (any string may be set; unknown placeholders are left in place and reported). Every template is written for offline teams and repeatable releases.

templates.name: Desktop-First Architecture Plan
templates.purpose: Plan a desktop-first application whose mobile/web variants, if any, are secondary targets reusing the core.
owners: Consulted: platform engineers (OS packaging), QA lead
prerequisites: Target OSes and minimum versions fixed (Windows/macOS/Linux)
Offline toolchain bundle verified on a clean machine with network blocked
Windowing strategy and form-factor baseline chosen (single window, multi-document, tray, kiosk)
Distribution route decided (store, direct download, enterprise MDM)
steps: Freeze scope: features must run 100% offline; networked features listed separately
Scaffold the app shell with pinned framework (see profile command output)
Implement core domain + local persistence with migration path
Add platform integrations behind stable interfaces (filesystem, notifications, tray, update check)
Wire packaging (MSIX/DMG/AppImage+deb/rpm) with checksums
Run acceptance checklist on each target OS on physical or VM hardware
Produce release record: artifacts, checksums, SBOM, rollback instructions
decision_points: Framework: native vs Qt vs Tauri vs Electron vs Avalonia (use the matrix command)
Update channel: store-managed vs self-hosted updates vs manual
Single binary vs modular install
failure_recovery: Build breaks after toolchain update: freeze to last known-good pin, re-verify on clean machine, then retry
Packaging rejected by store: fall back to direct signed distribution, log policy delta, plan compliance fix
Data migration failure on upgrade: abort before commit, restore backup, ship forward-only fix release
evidence: Clean-machine build log with network blocked
Acceptance report per OS (accept command output)
Artifacts + SHA-256 manifest + SBOM + license manifest
templates.completion_condition: Installer built from the offline bundle launches on every target OS from a clean machine with network blocked, passes the acceptance checklist, and can be rolled back to the previous version without data loss.

templates.name: Mobile-First Architecture Plan
templates.purpose: Plan a mobile-first application (Android/iOS) with optional desktop later, optimizing for touch, offline, and store policies.
prerequisites: Minimum API/OS levels chosen; target devices enumerated (low-end to flagship)
Offline toolchain bundle verified (Android SDK/Gradle cache or Xcode/SPM mirror)
Physical devices reserved for camera/mic/GPS/biometrics/background/notification acceptance
Store accounts exist or are created before release milestones
steps: Freeze offline-first scope; define degradation for any networked feature
Scaffold app with pinned toolchain; commit lockfile and dependency hashes
Implement persistence + migrations; test upgrade from N-1 and N-2 versions
Implement permission-gated features behind interfaces with mocked offline tests
Background work, notifications, and battery/thermal budgets defined and measured
Accessibility pass: TalkBack/VoiceOver, 200% font scale, focus order
Release: AAB/IPA signed, reproducible where platform permits, store submission via connected environment
decision_points: Native (Compose/SwiftUI) vs Flutter vs KMP vs React Native (use the matrix command)
Play App Signing vs self-signed APK route (iOS: App Store vs ad hoc/enterprise)
Target SDK policy risk acceptance vs upgrading dependencies now
failure_recovery: Store rejection: remediate against written policy, resubmit; do not ship policy workarounds
Crash on low-end device class: gate feature by device capability, hotfix via expedited review only if data-loss class
Migration corrupts on-device data: halt rollout, restore from encrypted backup, ship forward migration fix with tests from the corrupted fixture
evidence: Clean-machine build log with network blocked
Device matrix test report (low-end + flagship, both ABIs where applicable)
Store submission receipt / signed artifact checksums
templates.completion_condition: Signed AAB/IPA built from the offline bundle installs and passes acceptance on representative physical devices of every declared class, including upgrade from the previous release with user data preserved.

templates.name: Universal Application Architecture Plan
templates.purpose: Plan one codebase for desktop + mobile (and optionally web), with per-platform shells over a shared core.
owners: Consulted: per-platform engineers, UX, release manager
prerequisites: Explicit per-platform acceptance matrix (what must work where)
Shared-core boundaries agreed (domain, persistence, sync vs platform UI/adapters)
Offline bundle covers ALL target toolchains; CI restores all before build
Universal binary / per-ABI distribution strategy decided
steps: Write the acceptance matrix first; if a platform cannot pass it, drop the platform, do not fork the app
Design module layout: core (pure, tested) / platform adapters (interfaces) / platform shells (thin)
Implement shared core with golden-file and contract tests
Implement per-platform shells and adapters; contract tests per adapter
Form-factor adaptation: windowing/responsive/tablet/foldable rules with tests
Per-platform packaging and signing pipelines sharing one release record
Run full acceptance checklist on every target on real hardware
decision_points: Flutter vs KMP+native UI vs Avalonia vs Uno vs Qt (matrix command; check accessibility scores)
Shared sync engine vs platform-native sync
Single train release vs per-platform trains
failure_recovery: One platform fails acceptance: hold its release, ship others, fix forward - never block all trains on one target's simulator
Shared core regression: contract tests catch it pre-merge; revert to last good core, re-run full matrix
Toolchain drift between targets: pin exact versions in one manifest; the verify command checks them
evidence: ADR for framework and train model
templates.completion_condition: Every platform in the acceptance matrix passes with network blocked on clean machines/devices, from one tagged source revision, with per-platform artifacts and rollback instructions.

templates.name: Clean Architecture Plan
templates.purpose: Plan dependency-inverted layering (entities -> use cases -> adapters -> frameworks) for testable offline apps.
prerequisites: Module/build system supports dependency rules enforcement (lint, import guard, or arch-test)
Domain glossary agreed; persistence and framework choices listed but NOT baked into entities
steps: Define entities and value objects (no outward imports)
Define use cases with ports (interfaces) for every I/O: storage, network, clock, identity, files
Implement gateway adapters; contract tests against the ports
Wire framework layer last; DI composition root per platform
Add architecture tests: import rules, cyclic-dependency ban, adapter conformance
Document the dependency rule and the escape-hatch policy for pragmatic violations
decision_points: Anemic vs rich entities
Ports on use-case side vs consumer-defined interfaces
Transaction boundary per use case (unit of work)
failure_recovery: Dependency rule violated in review: block merge; move code behind the port, never import outward
Use case grows orchestration logic: split by transaction boundary; extract domain service
Framework upgrade ripples inward: only composition root may change; ports isolate the blast radius
evidence: Architecture test output (import rules) passing in CI
Dependency graph artifact (e.g. tools-generated module graph)
ADR documenting layering and any sanctioned violations
templates.completion_condition: Domain module builds with zero outward dependencies, architecture tests pass in CI, and every external dependency is reachable only through a port with a contract test.

templates.name: Hexagonal (Ports and Adapters) Plan
templates.purpose: Plan ports/adapters decomposition so storage, network, and device capabilities are swappable and fully mockable offline.
prerequisites: List of every external capability the app needs (drive at least storage, identity, clock, network)
Offline test strategy agreed: adapters must be runnable against in-memory fakes
steps: Define primary (driving) ports: UI actions and external events as typed commands/queries
Define secondary (driven) ports: repositories, gateways, notifiers, key stores
Implement in-memory adapters first; tests green before any real adapter exists
Implement real adapters (SQLite, filesystem, platform keystore) behind the same ports
Contract tests: every adapter passes the same suite; fakes and real adapters both run
Document adapter selection per platform and the degradation order when a capability is missing
decision_points: Sync engine as port vs internal detail
One generic repository port vs per-aggregate ports
In-memory fake vs SQLite-backed test double
failure_recovery: Adapter cannot satisfy the port offline (e.g. push): declare explicit unsupported state, degrade, never fake success
Contract drift between fake and real adapter: CI runs both suites; a green fake with a red real adapter blocks release
evidence: Contract test matrix (fake vs real, per platform)
Port catalog with owner, fallback, and offline behavior
ADR for adapter selection per platform
templates.completion_condition: All external capabilities behind ports; contract suite green for every real adapter on its target platform; in-memory fakes pass tests with the network blocked.

templates.name: Offline-First Product Requirements Builder
templates.purpose: Author the product requirements document from pinned local inputs with integrity checks, so requirements are reproducible and reviewable offline.
prerequisites: Inputs collected as local files: prior PRDs, ADRs, acceptance reference, store/enterprise policies
Input manifest with SHA-256 of every source (use verify --init-manifest)
Constraint register seeded (offline, signing, distribution, compliance)
steps: Verify input manifest before drafting; reject on hash mismatch
Capture goals and NON-goals; list networked features with offline degradation for each
Enumerate constraints: platform, toolchain, licensing, signing, privacy, accessibility, store policy
Define quality bars: performance budgets, a11y criteria, localization scope, offline test coverage
Write acceptance matrix skeleton (input to the acceptance-signoff template)
Review on paper/PDF offline; record decisions as ADRs; archive the verified inputs with the PRD
decision_points: What is explicitly out of scope for offline (store submission packet, push, payments) and how each degrades
Which platforms are in the release trains
Quality bar sign-off authority
failure_recovery: Input contradicts itself: log the conflict as a decision point; do not silently pick one
Requirement unverifiable: mark blocked, add verification method or drop the requirement
Hash mismatch on an input: stop, re-obtain the input from its owner, re-verify, restart drafting
templates.completion_condition: PRD archive contains verified inputs, every requirement is testable or removed, every networked feature has a written offline degradation, and the acceptance matrix is ready for sign-off planning.

templates.name: Proof-of-Concept Spine Builder
templates.purpose: Build the thinnest end-to-end spine (input -> domain -> storage -> UI -> packaging) that installs and launches offline, before feature work.
prerequisites: Framework selected (matrix command + ADR)
Offline toolchain bundle verified
One representative user journey chosen (not a toy)
steps: Scaffold minimal app shell; no features
Implement ONE real persistence path (write + read + migrate) with a migration test
Implement ONE real UI path exercising the persistence
Wire local packaging; install and launch on a clean machine/device with network blocked
Add smoke test that fails loudly; wire into CI restore-build-test
Freeze the spine; cut the tag; all feature work builds on it
decision_points: Which single journey proves the spine
Migration engine choice now vs later
CI runner offline capability
failure_recovery: Spine cannot install on target: stop all feature work; fix the bundle/packaging until it passes; partial features on a broken spine are wasted work
Migration test fails: rollback to empty schema v1, implement migration correctly, re-tag
evidence: ADR for stack and persistence choices
templates.completion_condition: A clean machine with network blocked installs the packaged spine, launches it, writes and reads one real record through a migration, and the CI smoke test passes on the tag.

templates.name: Maintenance Release Planner
templates.purpose: Plan a patch/maintenance release with controlled risk, reproducible build, and verified rollback.
prerequisites: Release branch cut from the shipped tag; hotfix cherry-picks only
Issue(s) reproduced and assigned; regression test written that fails on main
Rollback target identified and artifacts available
steps: Reproduce with the regression test; confirm fix on branch
Run full affected suite + acceptance checklist on the release candidate
Build reproducible artifact; verify SHA-256 against rebuild if platform permits
Stage rollout (internal -> beta -> broad) with explicit go/no-go gates
Monitor crash/diagnostic signals; rollback trigger pre-agreed with a time box
Retro-write the ADR/RCA; feed systemic fixes into next minor release
decision_points: Ship now vs wait for next scheduled release
Rollback vs forward-fix if the candidate fails acceptance
Expedited store review request (only for data-loss/security classes)
failure_recovery: Candidate fails acceptance: abort release, revert the hotfix, schedule forward fix
Field regression detected post-release: execute pre-agreed rollback to prior artifact, halt staged rollout
Rebuild mismatch (non-reproducible): investigate before shipping anything; non-reproducibility is itself a defect
evidence: Regression test id and CI link
templates.completion_condition: Patch released through the staged rollout with the pre-agreed rollback armed, acceptance report attached, and RCA archived; or cleanly aborted with the branch restored.

templates.name: Upgrade and Migration Plan
templates.purpose: Plan a risky upgrade: SDK, framework, database schema, OS floor, or dependency with breaking changes.
prerequisites: Current state inventoried: exact versions, schema hash, config surface
Backup/restore tested on a production-like snapshot
Offline bundle for the NEW toolchain verified before any code change
steps: Inventory and baseline: capture versions, golden outputs, benchmark numbers
Load the new bundle; build unmodified source; catalog compile breaks
Migrate in layers: build -> test -> data -> behavior; one layer per commit
Database: write forward + backward migrations; test from N-2, N-1, and corrupted fixtures
Re-run benchmarks; compare against budgets; investigate any regression
Full acceptance checklist; stage rollout with rollback armed
decision_points: Big-bang vs incremental (strangler) migration
Minimum supported source version (N-2 vs N-1)
Dual-write period for migrations touching sync
failure_recovery: Migration fails mid-upgrade on device: abort before commit point, restore backup, report; never half-migrate
Performance regression > budget: block release; profile; optimize or negotiate the budget with an ADR
New toolchain cannot be restored offline: abort upgrade entirely until the bundle is complete
templates.completion_condition: Upgraded build passes the full acceptance checklist on clean machines and physical devices for upgrade paths from N-2 and N-1, with data preserved and rollback rehearsed, under the staged rollout.

templates.name: Rollback and Recovery Plan
templates.purpose: Plan for shipping and executing rollback when a release goes wrong, including data-format rollback.
owners: Consulted: on-call, support, legal/privacy if data involved
prerequisites: Previous known-good artifacts retained and checksummed
Rollback trigger criteria written BEFORE release (crash rate, data errors, install failures)
Data backward-compatibility verified (new format readable by old build, or dual-write)
steps: Detect: monitoring thresholds or user reports escalated into the release channel
Decide within the time box: rollback vs forward-fix (forward-fix only for trivial, proven patches)
Halt staged rollout and any store phased release
Execute rollback: re-sign/point update channel at previous artifact (stores obey store mechanics - plan for store latency)
Verify field recovery: metrics return to baseline; support confirms
Post-incident review; file defect; feed fixes into maintenance-release template
decision_points: Rollback vs forward-fix (time-boxed, data-safety first)
Store rollback limitations: can prior version re-roll-out? Phasing pauses are the lever when binary rollback is impossible
Data restore vs quarantine for unreadable records
failure_recovery: Rollback impossible for store release: pause rollout, communicate, forward-fix expedited; learn the constraint for next release
Data already migrated and incompatible: ship recovery build that upgrades-forward only; never attempt destructive downgrade
Rollback itself fails integrity check: quarantine the release channel; escalate to incident process
evidence: Recovery metrics (crash-free rate, error rate) vs baseline
templates.completion_condition: Field metrics back to pre-release baseline, all affected users on a known-good build, incident review archived, and the release criteria updated so the same failure mode is caught pre-release next time.

templates.name: Target Device Acceptance Sign-off Plan
templates.purpose: Plan the acceptance evaluation per target device/simulator and the sign-off gate for release, per the catalog's acceptance reference.
prerequisites: Acceptance checklist finalized (accept --init-results from asset-acceptance-checklist.json)
Devices/emulators provisioned: low-end + flagship per platform, real hardware for hardware-dependent features
Build under test tagged; environment (OS, SDK, toolchain) recorded
steps: Enumerate the acceptance matrix: platform x device class x checklist
Execute checks on each cell; record pass/warn/fail with evidence (logs, screenshots)
Triage warns: accept with documented rationale or convert to fix+retest within the time box
Any fail halts sign-off; remediation retest scoped to the failed cells plus regression sweep
Aggregate report; release manager signs or rejects with written reasons
Archive report with the release record; feed gaps into the next planning cycle
decision_points: Ship with documented warns vs hold
Device class coverage vs time budget
Simulator-only coverage acceptable for which check rows
failure_recovery: Late fail on one device class: hold that class's train; do not ship partial matrix as 'accepted'
Cannot reproduce fail in clean environment: keep the cell as UNTESTED, never as pass; escalate with evidence
Sign-off dispute: defer to the pre-agreed criterion table, not to seniority
evidence: accept command report per device cell (retained)
Checksums of the exact binaries installed
Registry of known warns with owners and due dates
templates.completion_condition: Every cell of the acceptance matrix is pass (or a documented, owned warn), zero fails, report retained in the release record, and the go/no-go decision written and signed.
